newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs seen stable, await industrial output data.
newsitem.headline: JGBs seen stable, await industrial output data.

text.p: JGBs are seen moving stably on Monday with the downside limited by the BOJ's cautious stance toward the economy in a report last week and the upside capped by the yen's fall over the weekend, traders said on Monday.
The Bank of Japan, in its quarterly economic outlook, showed a cautious attitude toward the economy, which last week boosted the key September contract to 126.02, the highest since April 25.
The market is keenly watching June industrial output data due on Wednesday, particularly the outlook for production in July and August, traders said.

After the BOJ's economic outlook, speculation was mounting that the central bank may not be able to raise the key official discount rate until next April, some traders said, as the BOJ may want to confirm the strength of spending during the October-November period, for which data would be available early next year.
Many think that the BOJ is unlikely to tighten credit in the February-March period, when most Japanese companies try to settle profit/loss figures in a run-up to end-March corporate book closings.
